evidence.finding: Orientation-preserving disk isometries are the Mobius transformations mapping the disk bijectively to itself; orientation-reversing cases involve conjugation. Strict radial scaling by a factor below one maps to a proper subdisk and changes radial hyperbolic distance.
Exact values, solution completeness, domain preservation and counterexamples are checked directly.

For real positive reference impedance and alpha*l>0, Gamma maps to a*exp(i phi)*Gamma with 0<a=exp(-2alpha*l)<1. A radial point r has disk distance 2*atanh(r) from zero; after the map this becomes 2*atanh(a*r), strictly smaller.

The passive positive-real impedance half-plane maps to the disk for a real positive reference impedance. Appropriate lossless maps can be isometries; the rejection concerns the unqualified claim including lossy cascades.

evidence.title: Mathematical and Computational Applications 28(4), 87, equations 1 and 10
evidence.finding: The primary beam-on-Winkler-foundation buckling equation is EI*v_fourth+Pc*v_second+kw*v=0; its squared characteristic roots have product kw/EI>0. This supports the narrow missing-model hold rather than excluding hyperbolic terms from every possible model.

For the standard compressed uniform Winkler model EI*w_fourth+P*w_second+k*w=0, characteristic r² values have product k/EI>0. A pure real pair ±beta and pure imaginary pair ±i*alpha would instead have negative product -alpha²*beta², so that simple mixed basis does not follow automatically.

This is a missing-model/evidence hold, not a claim that no column model can ever involve cosh. Complex-root foundation regimes can have hyperbolic-trigonometric products with different characteristic conditions.

records.rationale: The fading-superposition description is sound, but unequal decay rates do not make exact destructive cancellation impossible at every instant. Envelopes with different starting amplitudes can cross; persistent cancellation is the stronger condition that generally fails.

evidence.finding: Opposite-phase amplitudes A1(t),A2(t) cancel exactly when A1(t)=A2(t). Different decay rates prevent persistent matching in general but do not prohibit an isolated equality.
Opposite-phase envelopes A1=exp(-t) and A2=2exp(-2t) are equal at t=ln2, both1/2, despite different decay rates. Their combined phasor is zero at that instant.

If unequal instantaneous amplitudes are intended, they indeed cannot cancel fully. Hold for ambiguity between unequal decay laws and unequal amplitudes at a given time, not for the linear superposition principle.
